q: Q1 ★ (MCQ, SQP; same idea 2023) The greatest number which divides both 134 and 188, leaving remainders 4 and 6 respectively, is: (A) 13 (B) 26 (C) 39 (D) 65
a: Ans: (B) 26. Subtract the remainders: 134 - 4 = 130 and 188 - 6 = 182. HCF(130, 182): 130 = 2 × 5 × 13, 182 = 2 × 7 × 13, so HCF = 2 × 13 = 26.

q: Q2 (MCQ, 2025) If HCF(98, 28) = m and LCM(98, 28) = n, then the value of n - 7m is: (A) 0 (B) 28 (C) 98 (D) 198
Q3 (MCQ, 2019) Two positive integers a and b can be written as a = x³y² and b = xy³, where x, y are prime numbers. Find LCM(a, b).
a: Ans: x³y³. LCM = product of the highest power of each prime. (HCF would be the lowest powers: xy².)

q: Q4 ★ (3 marks, 2019; √5 in 2023) Prove that √2 is an irrational number.
a:
Ans:

  • Suppose √2 is rational. Then √2 = a/b, where a and b are co-prime integers and b ≠ 0.
  • Squaring: 2 = a²/b², so a² = 2b². So 2 divides a², hence 2 divides a. Let a = 2c.
  • Then 4c² = 2b², so b² = 2c². So 2 divides b², hence 2 divides b.
  • Now 2 divides both a and b. This contradicts that a and b are co-prime.
  • So our assumption is wrong. √2 is irrational. (For √3 or √5, replace 2 by 3 or 5 in every line.)

q: Q5 ★ (3 marks, SQP; 2 + 3√5 in 2026; (2 + √3)/5 in 2019) Given that √3 is irrational, prove that (2 + 3√3) is irrational.
a:
Ans:

  • Suppose 2 + 3√3 is rational. Then 2 + 3√3 = p/q, where p, q are integers, q ≠ 0.
  • So 3√3 = p/q - 2 = (p - 2q)/q, and √3 = (p - 2q)/(3q).
  • The right side is rational (integers divided by a non-zero integer), so √3 would be rational.
  • But √3 is irrational. This is a contradiction. So 2 + 3√3 is irrational.

q: Q6 ★ (2 marks, SQP) Three bells toll at intervals of 5, 6 and 8 minutes. They all toll together at 10:00 a.m. when the park opens. How many more times do they toll together till the park closes at 7:00 p.m.?
a:
Ans:

  • LCM(5, 6, 8): 5 = 5, 6 = 2 × 3, 8 = 2³. LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 = 120 minutes = 2 hours.
  • They toll together every 2 hours: 12 noon, 2 p.m., 4 p.m., 6 p.m. (8 p.m. is after closing).
  • So they toll together 4 more times. (Other OR in SQP: hall 9.75 m × 6.75 m × 5.25 m, longest ruler = HCF(975, 675, 525) cm = 75 cm.)

q: Q7 ★ (MCQ, SQP) If f(x) = px² + qx + r, p ≠ 0 and p + r = q, then one of the zeroes of f(x) is: (A) q/p (B) r/p (C) -r/p (D) -q/p
a: Ans: (C) -r/p. Put x = -1: f(-1) = p - q + r = 0 (because q = p + r). So -1 is a zero. Product of zeroes = r/p, so the other zero = (r/p) ÷ (-1) = -r/p.

q: Q8 ★ (A-R, SQP) A: If the zeroes of (2k - 1)x² + 4x - 3 are reciprocal of each other, then k = -1. R: If a = c, then the zeroes of ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0) are reciprocal of each other.
a: Ans: (A) Both true and R explains A. Reciprocal zeroes means product = 1, so c/a = 1, i.e. a = c: 2k - 1 = -3, k = -1.

q: Q9 (A-R, 2024) A: If the graph of a polynomial touches the x-axis at only one point, then the polynomial cannot be a quadratic polynomial. R: A polynomial of degree n (n > 1) can have at most n zeroes.
a: Ans: (D) A is false (y = x² touches the x-axis only at (0, 0) and is quadratic). R is true.

q: Q10 ★ (3 marks, 2019) Find the value of k such that the polynomial x² - (k + 6)x + 2(2k - 1) has sum of its zeroes equal to half of their product.
a:
Ans:

  • a = 1, b = -(k + 6), c = 2(2k - 1)
  • Sum = -b/a = k + 6; Product = c/a = 2(2k - 1)
  • k + 6 = ½ × 2(2k - 1) = 2k - 1
  • k = 7

(SQP similar, 3 marks: if α, β are zeroes of 2x² - 8x + 5, find (α + 1/β)(β + 1/α). Expand: αβ + 1 + 1 + 1/(αβ). αβ = 5/2, so the value = 5/2 + 2 + 2/5 = 49/10.)

q: Q11 (MCQ, 2025) If x = 1 and y = 2 is a solution of the pair of linear equations 2x - 3y + a = 0 and 2x + 3y - b = 0, then: (A) a = 2b (B) 2a = b (C) a + 2b = 0 (D) 2a + b = 0
a: Ans: (B) 2a = b. Put x = 1, y = 2: 2 - 6 + a = 0 gives a = 4; 2 + 6 - b = 0 gives b = 8. So b = 2a.

chapter: Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
q: Q12 ★ (2 marks, 2019) Find c if the system cx + 3y + (3 - c) = 0, 12x + cy - c = 0 has infinitely many solutions.
a:
Ans:

  • Condition: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2, so c/12 = 3/c = (3 - c)/(-c)
  • c/12 = 3/c gives c² = 36, c = ±6
  • 3/c = (3 - c)/(-c) gives -3 = 3 - c, so c = 6
  • c = 6 (satisfies both) (Remember: unique solution a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2; no solution a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2.)

chapter: Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
q: Q13 (2 marks, 2024) Solve 7x - 2y = 5 and 8x + 7y = 15 and verify your answer.
a:
Ans (elimination):

  • Multiply the first by 7: 49x - 14y = 35. Multiply the second by 2: 16x + 14y = 30.
  • Add: 65x = 65, so x = 1. Then 7(1) - 2y = 5, so y = 1.
  • Verify: 7 - 2 = 5 ✓ and 8 + 7 = 15 ✓.

chapter: Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
q: Q14 ★ (3 marks, 2019) A father's age is three times the sum of the ages of his two children. After 5 years his age will be two times the sum of their ages. Find the present age of the father.
a:
Ans:

  • Let father = x years, sum of children's ages = y years. So x = 3y.
  • After 5 years: father x + 5; children's sum y + 10 (each child gets 5 years older).
  • x + 5 = 2(y + 10), so x - 2y = 15. Put x = 3y: y = 15.
  • Father = 45 years.

chapter: Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
q: Q15 ★ (5 marks, 2025) Vijay invested money in two schemes A and B at 8% and 9% per annum. He received ₹1,860 total annual interest. Had he interchanged the amounts, he would have received ₹20 more. How much did he invest in each scheme?
a:
Ans:

  • Let ₹x in A and ₹y in B. 8x/100 + 9y/100 = 1860, so 8x + 9y = 186000 ...(1)
  • Interchanged: 9x + 8y = 188000 ...(2)
  • Add: 17x + 17y = 374000, so x + y = 22000 ...(3)
  • Subtract (1) from (2): x - y = 2000 ...(4)
  • From (3) and (4): x = 12000, y = 10000.
  • ₹12,000 in scheme A and ₹10,000 in scheme B. (SQP case study similar: x + y = 1000 and 10x + 15y = 12750 give 450 small and 550 large bottles in June.)

q: Q16 ★ (MCQ, SQP) If (1 - p) is a root of x² + px + 1 - p = 0, then its roots are: (A) 0, 1 (B) -1, 1 (C) 0, -1 (D) -1, 2
a: Ans: (C) 0, -1. Put x = 1 - p: (1 - p)² + p(1 - p) + (1 - p) = (1 - p)(1 - p + p + 1) = 2(1 - p) = 0, so p = 1. The equation becomes x² + x = 0, i.e. x(x + 1) = 0, roots 0 and -1.

q: Q17 ★ (2 marks, 2017) Find the value of k for which x² + k(2x + k - 1) + 2 = 0 has real and equal roots.
a:
Ans:

  • x² + 2kx + (k² - k + 2) = 0. So a = 1, b = 2k, c = k² - k + 2.
  • Equal roots: D = b² - 4ac = 0
  • 4k² - 4(k² - k + 2) = 0, so 4k - 8 = 0
  • k = 2 (2019 MCQ: for real roots of x² + 4x + k = 0, D ≥ 0 gives 16 - 4k ≥ 0, so k ≤ 4.)

q: Q18 (2 marks, 2026) Verify that the roots of (p - q)x² + (q - r)x + (r - p) = 0 are equal when q + r = 2p.
a:
Ans:

  • D = (q - r)² - 4(p - q)(r - p)
  • If q + r = 2p, then r = 2p - q, so q - r = 2q - 2p = -2(p - q) and r - p = p - q.
  • D = 4(p - q)² - 4(p - q)(p - q) = 0. So the roots are equal.

q: Q19 ★ (5 marks, 2025) A train travels 480 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 8 km/h less, it would have taken 3 hours more. Find the speed of the train.
a:
Ans:

  • Let speed = x km/h. Time = 480/x. New time = 480/(x - 8).
  • 480/(x - 8) - 480/x = 3
  • 480 × 8 = 3x(x - 8), so 3840 = 3x² - 24x, so x² - 8x - 1280 = 0
  • (x - 40)(x + 32) = 0, so x = 40 or -32 (speed cannot be negative)
  • Speed = 40 km/h

q: Q20 ★ (5 marks, SQP) A rectangular park is 50 m × 40 m. A rectangular pool is built in the middle with a grass strip of uniform width around it. The area of the grass strip is 1184 m². Find the dimensions of the pool.
a:
Ans:

  • Let the strip width = x m. Pool = (50 - 2x) by (40 - 2x).
  • Pool area = 2000 - 1184 = 816 m²
  • (50 - 2x)(40 - 2x) = 816, so 4x² - 180x + 2000 = 816, so x² - 45x + 296 = 0
  • (x - 8)(x - 37) = 0. x = 37 is impossible (50 - 74 < 0), so x = 8.
  • Pool = 34 m × 24 m (check: 34 × 24 = 816 ✓) (Also asked: 2019 taps fill a tank in 15/8 h, one takes 2 h less → 3 h and 5 h; 2026 tour ₹5,400, extend 5 days, cut ₹180/day → x² + 5x - 150 = 0 → 10 days, ₹540/day; 2025 right triangle perimeter 60 cm, hypotenuse 25 cm → sides 15 cm and 20 cm.)

q: Q21 (MCQ, SQP) The middle term of the AP 10, 7, 4, ..., -62 is: (A) -26 (B) -29 (C) -32 (D) -35
Q22 ★ (MCQ, 2025; S_n given in 2019 too) If the sum of the first m terms of an AP is 2m² + 3m, then its second term is: (A) 10 (B) 9 (C) 12 (D) 4
a: Ans: (B) 9. S1 = 2 + 3 = 5 = a1. S2 = 8 + 6 = 14. a2 = S2 - S1 = 9. (2019: if S_n = 3n² - 4n, then a_n = S_n - S_(n-1) = 6n - 7.)

q: Q23 ★ (2 marks, 2019; same type 2017) How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 3?
a:
Ans:

  • AP: 12, 15, 18, ..., 99. a = 12, d = 3, a_n = 99
  • 99 = 12 + (n - 1) × 3, so (n - 1) = 29, n = 30 (2019 Set III: two-digit numbers divisible by 7: 14, ..., 98 gives 13. 2017: integers between 200 and 500 divisible by 8: 208, ..., 496 gives 37.)

q: Q24 ★ (2 marks, 2019) Which term of the AP 3, 15, 27, 39, ... will be 120 more than its 21st term?
a:
Ans:

  • a = 3, d = 12. a21 = 3 + 20 × 12 = 243
  • Required term = 243 + 120 = 363 = 3 + (n - 1) × 12, so n - 1 = 30
  • 31st term

q: Q25 (3 marks, SQP) Find the sum of integers between 1 and 400 that are multiples of 4 as well as of 5.
a:
Ans:

  • Multiples of both 4 and 5 = multiples of 20: 20, 40, ..., 380 (400 is not "between")
  • 380 = 20 + (n - 1) × 20, so n = 19
  • S19 = 19/2 × (20 + 380) = 19 × 200 = 3800

q: Q26 ★ (Case study 4 marks, 2025) A charity run: the first round is 300 m and each next round is 50 m longer. There are 10 rounds. (i) Write the 4th, 5th and 6th terms. (ii) Find the distance of the 8th round. (iii)(a) Total distance after 10 rounds. OR (iii)(b) Total distance of the first 6 rounds.
a:
Ans:

  • (i) a = 300, d = 50: 450 m, 500 m, 550 m
  • (ii) a8 = 300 + 7 × 50 = 650 m
  • (iii)(a) S10 = 10/2 [2 × 300 + 9 × 50] = 5 × 1050 = 5250 m
  • (iii)(b) S6 = 6/2 [600 + 5 × 50] = 3 × 850 = 2550 m (2026 "Kolam" case: 4, 8, 12, ... dots; a = 4, d = 4, a_n = 4n; S_n = 2n(n + 1) = 220 gives n = 10 squares; 2n(n + 1) = 100 has no whole-number answer, so 100 dots is not possible.)

q: Q27 (MCQ, SQP) The perimeters of two similar triangles are 56 cm and 70 cm. If one side of the first triangle is 14 cm, the corresponding side of the second is: (A) 5 (B) 7.5 (C) 10 (D) 17.5
a: Ans: (D) 17.5. Ratio of perimeters = ratio of sides: 14/x = 56/70, so x = 14 × 70/56 = 17.5 cm.

q: Q28 (MCQ, 2025) In triangles ABC and DEF, ∠B = ∠E, ∠F = ∠C and AB = 3DE. Then the two triangles are: (A) congruent but not similar (B) congruent as well as similar (C) neither congruent nor similar (D) similar but not congruent
a: Ans: (D). Two equal angles give similarity (AA). Sides are in ratio 3 : 1, so they are not congruent. (2025 Section B similar: if ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, AB = 6, BC = 4, AC = 8 and PR = 6 cm, the ratio is 6/8 = 3/4, so PQ = 4.5, QR = 3 and PQ + QR = 7.5 cm.)

q: Q29 ★ (5 marks, SQP; BPT used in 2023 and 2026 MCQs/short answers) Prove that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, divides the other two sides in the same ratio (Basic Proportionality Theorem).
a:
Ans:

  • Given: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB and E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC.
  • Construction: Join BE and CD. Draw EN ⟂ AB and DM ⟂ AC.
  • ar(ADE) = ½ × AD × EN, ar(BDE) = ½ × DB × EN. So ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB ...(1)
  • ar(ADE) = ½ × AE × DM, ar(DEC) = ½ × EC × DM. So ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC ...(2)
  • ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so ar(BDE) = ar(DEC) ...(3)
  • From (1), (2), (3): AD/DB = AE/EC. Hence proved.
  • Draw the figure (triangle with DE parallel to BC, the two joins and two perpendiculars). The figure alone carries marks.

q: Q30 ★ (2 marks, SQP) ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Its diagonals meet at O. Show that AO/BO = CO/DO.
a:
Ans:

  • In ΔAOB and ΔCOD: ∠OAB = ∠OCD (alternate angles, AB ∥ DC) and ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite).
  • So ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (AA). Hence AO/CO = BO/DO.
  • Rearranging: AO/BO = CO/DO. (SQP OR: if ∠PQR = ∠QSP, PQ = 6 cm, PS = 3 cm, then ΔPRQ ~ ΔPQS, so PQ/PR = PS/PQ, 36 = 3 × PR, PR = 12 cm.)

q: Q31 ★ (MCQ, SQP and 2024) PM is a median of ΔPQR with vertices P(5, -6), Q(6, 4) and R(0, 0). The length of PM is: (A) 2√17 (B) 2√15 (C) √101 (D) 10 units
Q32 (MCQ, SQP) The point which lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining A(-3, -4) and B(3, 4) is: (A) (0, 0) (B) (0, 3) (C) (3, 0) (D) (0, 4)
a: Ans: (A) (0, 0). It is the mid-point of AB, and the mid-point lies on the perpendicular bisector.

q: Q33 (MCQ, 2024; same type 2017) If the distance between (3, -5) and (x, -5) is 15 units, then x is: (A) 12, -18 (B) -12, 18 (C) 18, 5 (D) -9, -12
a: Ans: (B). √[(x - 3)² + 0] = 15, so x - 3 = ±15, x = 18 or -12. (2017: distance between (4, k) and (1, 0) is 5 gives 9 + k² = 25, k = ±4.)

q: Q34 ★ (3 marks, SQP; same type 2019, 2023) In what ratio does the x-axis divide the line segment joining (-4, -6) and (-1, 7)? Find the point of division.
a:
Ans:

  • Let the ratio be k : 1. The point on the x-axis has y = 0.
  • y = (k × 7 + 1 × (-6))/(k + 1) = 0, so 7k = 6, k = 6/7. Ratio 6 : 7.
  • x = (6 × (-1) + 7 × (-4))/(6 + 7) = (-6 - 28)/13 = -34/13
  • Point = (-34/13, 0) (2019: x-axis divides (1, -3) and (4, 5) in ratio 3 : 5 at (17/8, 0).)

q: Q35 ★ (3 marks, 2025; NCERT) Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the line segment joining (5, -6) and (-1, -4). Also find the point of intersection.
a:
Ans:

  • On the y-axis x = 0. Let ratio k : 1: x = (k × (-1) + 5)/(k + 1) = 0, so k = 5. Ratio 5 : 1.
  • y = (5 × (-4) + 1 × (-6))/6 = -26/6 = -13/3
  • Point = (0, -13/3)

q: Q36 (3 marks, 2019) Find the point on the y-axis which is equidistant from (5, -2) and (-3, 2).
a:
Ans:

  • Let P = (0, y). PA² = PB²: 25 + (y + 2)² = 9 + (y - 2)²
  • 25 + y² + 4y + 4 = 9 + y² - 4y + 4, so 8y = -16, y = -2
  • P = (0, -2)

q: Q37 ★ (A-R, SQP) A: If three vertices of a parallelogram taken in order are (-1, -6), (2, -5) and (7, 2), then its fourth vertex is (4, 1). R: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
a: Ans: (A) Both true and R explains A. Mid-point of AC = ((-1 + 7)/2, (-6 + 2)/2) = (3, -2) = mid-point of BD. So D = (2 × 3 - 2, 2 × (-2) + 5) = (4, 1). (2019 1-mark: centre (2, -3), one end B(1, 4) of a diameter; other end A = (2 × 2 - 1, 2 × (-3) - 4) = (3, -10).)

q: Q38 (MCQ, 2025) If θ is an acute angle and 7 + 4 sin θ = 9, then θ is: (A) 90° (B) 30° (C) 45° (D) 60°
a: Ans: (B) 30°. 4 sin θ = 2, so sin θ = 1/2, θ = 30°.

q: Q39 ★ (MCQ, SQP) If tan(A + B) = √3 and tan(A - B) = 1/√3, 0° < A + B < 90°, A > B, then A and B are: (A) 60°, 30° (B) 60°, 45° (C) 45°, 15° (D) 60°, 15°
a: Ans: (C) 45°, 15°. A + B = 60° and A - B = 30°. Adding: 2A = 90°, A = 45°, B = 15°.

q: Q40 (MCQ, 2024) If sec θ - tan θ = m, then sec θ + tan θ = ?
a: Ans: 1/m. Because (sec θ - tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ - tan²θ = 1.

q: Q41 ★ (2 marks, 2024) Evaluate: 2√2 cos 45° sin 30° + 2√3 cos 30°.
Q42 ★ (2 marks, SQP) If tan θ = 1/√5, find the value of (cosec²θ - sec²θ)/(cosec²θ + sec²θ).
a:
Ans:

  • cot θ = √5, so cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ = 1 + 5 = 6
  • sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ = 1 + 1/5 = 6/5
  • Value = (6 - 6/5)/(6 + 6/5) = (24/5)/(36/5) = 2/3

q: Q43 ★ (3 marks, 2019) Prove that (sin θ + cosec θ)² + (cos θ + sec θ)² = 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ.
a:
Ans:

  • LHS = sin²θ + cosec²θ + 2 sin θ cosec θ + cos²θ + sec²θ + 2 cos θ sec θ
  • sin θ cosec θ = 1 and cos θ sec θ = 1, so LHS = (sin²θ + cos²θ) + cosec²θ + sec²θ + 2 + 2
  • = 1 + (1 + cot²θ) + (1 + tan²θ) + 4
  • = 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ = RHS. Hence proved.

q: Q44 ★ (3 marks, SQP) A student simplified cos θ/(1 - sin θ) + (1 - sin θ)/cos θ as follows: Step 1: [cos²θ + (1 - sin θ)²] / [(1 - sin θ) cos θ]; Step 2: [cos²θ + cos²θ] / [(1 - sin θ) cos θ]; Step 3: 2cos²θ / [(1 - sin θ) cos θ]; Step 4: 2cos θ/(1 - sin θ). Find the error and the correct answer.
a:
Ans:

  • Error in Step 2: (1 - sin θ)² is NOT cos²θ. (1 - sin²θ = cos²θ, but (1 - sin θ)² = 1 - 2 sin θ + sin²θ.)
  • Correct: numerator = cos²θ + 1 - 2 sin θ + sin²θ = 1 + 1 - 2 sin θ = 2(1 - sin θ)
  • So the expression = 2(1 - sin θ)/[(1 - sin θ) cos θ] = 2/cos θ = 2 sec θ

q: Q45 (3 marks, 2023) Prove that (tan θ + sec θ - 1)/(tan θ - sec θ + 1) = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
a:
Ans:

  • Write 1 = sec²θ - tan²θ in the numerator: tan θ + sec θ - (sec²θ - tan²θ)
  • = (sec θ + tan θ) - (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ - tan θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 - sec θ + tan θ)
  • Denominator = (tan θ - sec θ + 1), the same bracket, so it cancels.
  • LHS = sec θ + tan θ = 1/cos θ + sin θ/cos θ = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = RHS.

q: Q46 (MCQ, 2025; 1-mark 2017) A kite is flying at a height of 150 m. Its string is inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The length of the string is: (A) 100 m (B) 300 m (C) 150 m (D) 150√3 m
a: Ans: (B) 300 m. sin 30° = height/string, so 1/2 = 150/L, L = 300 m. (2017: tower : shadow = √3 : 1, so tan θ = √3, angle of elevation of the sun = 60°. SQP: string 52 m with tan θ = 12/5, so sin θ = 12/13 and height = 52 × 12/13 = 48 m.)

chapter: Chapter 9: Some Applications of Trigonometry (Heights and Distances)
q: Q47 ★ (5 marks, SQP) The angles of depression of two ships from the top of a lighthouse, on the same side, are 45° and 30°. The ships are 200 m apart, one exactly behind the other. Find the height of the lighthouse.
a:
Ans:

  • Let height = h, distance of the nearer ship = x. Draw the figure (lighthouse, two ships on a line).
  • Near ship (45°): tan 45° = h/x, so x = h.
  • Far ship (30°): tan 30° = h/(x + 200), so x + 200 = h√3.
  • h + 200 = h√3, so h(√3 - 1) = 200, h = 200/(√3 - 1) = 200(√3 + 1)/2 = 100(√3 + 1)
  • h = 100(√3 + 1) ≈ 273.2 m

chapter: Chapter 9: Some Applications of Trigonometry (Heights and Distances)
q: Q48 ★ (4 marks, 2019; 2017 same idea with a 150 m cliff) A man in a boat rowing away from a 100 m high lighthouse takes 2 minutes to change the angle of elevation of its top from 60° to 30°. Find the speed of the boat (√3 = 1.732).
a:
Ans:

  • First position: tan 60° = 100/d1, so d1 = 100/√3
  • Second position: tan 30° = 100/d2, so d2 = 100√3
  • Distance moved = 100√3 - 100/√3 = (300 - 100)/√3 = 200/√3 = 115.47 m
  • Speed = 115.47/2 = 57.73 m per minute

chapter: Chapter 9: Some Applications of Trigonometry (Heights and Distances)
q: Q49 ★ (3 marks, 2017 Set II) From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Find the height of the tower.
a:
Ans:

  • Depression 45° to the foot: distance between building and tower = 7 m (tan 45° = 7/d).
  • Elevation 60° to the top: extra height above the building level = 7 tan 60° = 7√3 m.
  • Tower = 7 + 7√3 = 7(√3 + 1) ≈ 19.12 m

chapter: Chapter 9: Some Applications of Trigonometry (Heights and Distances)
q: Q50 (5 marks, 2026) A kite is flying 60 m above the ground. Ravi, on the roof of a house, holds the string straight and sees the kite at an angle of elevation of 30°. From the bottom of the same building the angle of elevation of the kite is 45°. Find the length of the string and the height of the roof (√3 = 1.73).
a:
Ans:

  • From the bottom (45°): horizontal distance to the kite = 60 m.
  • From the roof (height r): tan 30° = (60 - r)/60, so 60 - r = 60/√3 = 20√3 = 34.6 m. Roof height r = 60 - 34.6 = 25.4 m.
  • String: sin 30° = (60 - r)/L, so L = 2 × 34.6 = 69.2 m (exactly 40√3 m). (2022 also asked: tower 50 m, elevation of the building top from the tower's foot 30°, of the tower top from the building's foot 60°; distance = 50/√3, building = (50/√3) × (1/√3) = 50/3 = 16.67 m.)

q: Q51 (MCQ, 2025; proof in 2017) The tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are always: (A) parallel (B) perpendicular (C) equal (D) intersecting
a: Ans: (A) parallel. Both tangents are ⟂ to the same diameter, so they are parallel (alternate angles 90° each).

q: Q52 (MCQ, 2026) PQ and PR are tangents to a circle with centre O and radius 4 cm such that ∠QPR = 90°. Then OP is: (A) 4 cm (B) 4√2 cm (C) 8 cm (D) 2√2 cm
a: Ans: (B) 4√2 cm. OQPR is a square of side 4 cm; OP is its diagonal = 4√2.

q: Q53 ★ (2 marks, 2025; same idea SQP case, 2022) A person standing at P is 26 m from the centre of a circular ground. His tangent distances PA and PB to the ground are 10 m each. Find the radius.
a:
Ans:

  • Radius ⟂ tangent, so ΔOAP is right-angled at A.
  • OA² = OP² - PA² = 26² - 10² = 676 - 100 = 576
  • Radius = 24 m (2022: concentric circles of radii 4 cm and 3 cm; chord of the bigger circle touching the smaller = 2√(16 - 9) = 2√7 cm.)

q: Q54 ★ (3 marks, NCERT theorem; used in every tangent question) Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
a:
Ans:

  • Given: PQ and PR are tangents from P to a circle with centre O. To prove: PQ = PR.
  • Join OP, OQ, OR. In ΔOQP and ΔORP:
  • OQ = OR (radii); OP = OP (common); ∠OQP = ∠ORP = 90° (radius ⟂ tangent)
  • So ΔOQP ≅ ΔORP (RHS). Hence PQ = PR (CPCT).

q: Q55 ★ (3 marks, 2017; 2023) Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point T. Prove that ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.
a:
Ans:

  • Let ∠PTQ = θ. TP = TQ (tangents from T), so ∠TPQ = ∠TQP = (180° - θ)/2 = 90° - θ/2.
  • ∠OPT = 90° (radius ⟂ tangent).
  • ∠OPQ = ∠OPT - ∠TPQ = 90° - (90° - θ/2) = θ/2.
  • So ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ. Hence proved.

q: Q56 ★ (3 marks, SQP) Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
a:
Ans:

  • Let ABCD be a parallelogram whose sides touch the circle at P (on AB), Q (BC), R (CD), S (DA).
  • Tangents from a point are equal: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS.
  • Add: (AP + BP) + (CR + DR) = (AS + DS) + (BQ + CQ), i.e. AB + CD = AD + BC.
  • In a parallelogram AB = CD and AD = BC, so 2AB = 2AD, AB = AD.
  • So all four sides are equal: ABCD is a rhombus.

q: Q57 ★ (Case study 4 marks, SQP) P is outside a circular garden with centre O and radius 9 m; OP = 18 m. PA and PB are tangents. (i) ∠OAP = ? (ii) Find PA. (iii)(A) Find ∠AOB. OR (iii)(B) If PA and PB were inclined at 60°, find their length.
a:
Ans:

  • (i) ∠OAP = 90° (radius ⟂ tangent)
  • (ii) PA = √(18² - 9²) = √(324 - 81) = √243 = 9√3 m
  • (iii)(A) cos ∠AOP = OA/OP = 9/18 = 1/2, so ∠AOP = 60°, and ∠AOB = 120°
  • (iii)(B) ∠APO = 30°, tan 30° = OA/PA, so PA = 9/(1/√3) = 9√3 m (2019: incircle of ΔABC with AB = 10, BC = 8, AC = 12 cm; using equal tangents x + y = 8, y + z = 12, x + z = 10 gives BL = 3, CM = 5, AN = 7 cm.)

q: Q58 ★ (MCQ, SQP) The diameter of a car wheel is 21 cm. The number of complete revolutions it makes in moving 66 km is: (A) 10⁴ (B) 10⁵ (C) 10⁶ (D) 10⁷
a: Ans: (B) 10⁵. Circumference = πd = 22/7 × 21 = 66 cm. 66 km = 66,00,000 cm. Revolutions = 66,00,000/66 = 1,00,000 = 10⁵. (In the printed SQP the options appear as "104, 105 ...": they mean powers of 10.)

q: Q59 ★ (MCQ, SQP) An arc of a circle is 6π cm long and the sector it bounds has area 24π cm². The radius is: (A) 4 (B) 8 (C) 16 (D) 18 cm
a: Ans: (B) 8 cm. Area of sector = ½ × arc length × r: 24π = ½ × 6π × r, so r = 8. (2025 MCQ: sector of area 40π sq. units and angle 72°: (72/360) πr² = 40π, r² = 200, r = 10√2.)

q: Q60 ★ (2 marks, SQP) Find the area of a sector of a circle with diameter 28 cm if the length of the corresponding arc is 22 cm.
a:
Ans:

  • r = 14 cm. Area of sector = ½ × l × r = ½ × 22 × 14 = 154 cm²
  • (Or: θ/360 × 2πr = 22 gives θ = 90°; area = ¼ × 22/7 × 196 = 154 cm².)

q: Q61 ★ (Case study 4 marks, 2025) A brooch is a circle of diameter 35 mm made of silver wire. 5 diameters divide it into 10 equal sectors. (i) Central angle of each sector? (ii) Length of arc ACB (one sector)? (iii)(a) Area of each sector? OR (iii)(b) Total length of silver wire?
a:
Ans:

  • (i) 360°/10 = 36°
  • (ii) Arc = circumference/10 = (22/7 × 35)/10 = 110/10 = 11 mm
  • (iii)(a) Sector area = (1/10) × 22/7 × 17.5 × 17.5 = 962.5/10 = 96.25 mm²
  • (iii)(b) Wire = circumference + 5 diameters = 110 + 5 × 35 = 285 mm

q: Q62 (3 marks, 2019 Set II; similar 2017) Find the area of the segment of a circle of radius 21 cm with ∠AOB = 120° (π = 22/7, √3 = 1.732).
a:
Ans:

  • Area of sector = 120/360 × 22/7 × 21 × 21 = 462 cm²
  • Area of ΔAOB = ½ r² sin 120° = ½ × 441 × (√3/2) = 441√3/4 = 190.95 cm²
  • Segment = 462 - 190.95 = 271.05 cm² (2017: chord subtending 60° in a circle of radius 10 cm, π = 3.14: sector 52.33, equilateral triangle (√3/4) × 100 = 43.30, minor segment ≈ 9.03 cm², major segment = 314 - 9.03 ≈ 304.97 cm².)

q: Q63 (MCQ, SQP) Two cubes, each of volume 64 cm³, are joined end to end. The surface area of the resulting cuboid is: (A) 192 (B) 160 (C) 96 (D) 80 cm²
Q64 (A-R, 2025) A: If we join two hemispheres of the same radius along their bases, we get a sphere. R: Total surface area of a sphere of radius r is 3πr².
a: Ans: (C) A is true; R is false (TSA of a sphere is 4πr²; 3πr² is the TSA of a solid hemisphere). (2024 MCQ: a solid sphere cut into two hemispheres; ratio of surface areas = 4πr² : 2 × 3πr² = 2 : 3. 2026 MCQ: three balls of radius r packed in a cylinder of radius r and height 6r; air = 6πr³ - 3 × (4/3)πr³ = 2πr³.)

q: Q65 ★ (5 marks, SQP) A tent is a cylinder (height 3 m, radius 14 m) surmounted by a cone. Total height is 13.5 m. Find the canvas needed, keeping 26 m² extra for stitching and wastage, and its cost at ₹250 per m².
a:
Ans:

  • Cone height = 13.5 - 3 = 10.5 m. Slant height l = √(14² + 10.5²) = √(196 + 110.25) = √306.25 = 17.5 m
  • CSA of cylinder = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 14 × 3 = 264 m²
  • CSA of cone = πrl = 22/7 × 14 × 17.5 = 770 m²
  • Canvas = 264 + 770 + 26 = 1060 m²
  • Cost = 1060 × 250 = ₹2,65,000
  • (No base: the floor of a tent is not covered with canvas.)

q: Q66 ★ (5 marks, SQP OR; 2022 similar) A solid toy is a hemisphere surmounted by a cone of the same radius 3.5 cm. Total volume is 166 5/6 cm³. Find the height of the cone, and the cost of painting the hemispherical part at ₹15 per cm².
a:
Ans:

  • Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ = 2/3 × 22/7 × 3.5³ = 539/6 cm³ (= 89 5/6)
  • Volume of cone = 1001/6 - 539/6 = 462/6 = 77 cm³
  • (1/3) × 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 × h = 77, so (77/6) h = 77, h = 6 cm
  • CSA of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm². Cost = 77 × 15 = ₹1,155 (2022: a cone of height 24 cm, radius 7 cm hollowed out of a cylinder of height 30 cm, radius 7 cm. TSA left = cylinder CSA 1320 + top circle 154 + cone CSA (l = 25) 550 = 2024 cm².)

q: Q67 ★ (MCQ, SQP; 2025, 2026 same idea) The mean and median of a data are 35.5 and 32. The mode is: (A) 23 (B) 26 (C) 25 (D) 30
a: Ans: (C) 25. Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean = 96 - 71 = 25. (2025: mode 15x, mean 18x gives median = (Mode + 2 Mean)/3 = (15x + 36x)/3 = 17x. 2026: mean 43, median 40 gives mode = 120 - 86 = 34.)

q: Q68 (MCQ, SQP) The mean age of a combined group of men and women is 35 years. The mean ages of men and women are 38 and 30 years. The percentage of women is: (A) 15 (B) 25.5 (C) 35 (D) 37.5
a: Ans: (D) 37.5. 38m + 30w = 35(m + w), so 3m = 5w, m : w = 5 : 3. Women = 3/8 = 37.5%.

q: Q69 ★ (Case study 4 marks, SQP) Marks (out of 50): 0-10: 3, 10-20: 6, 20-30: 12, 30-40: 15, 40-50: 14. (i) Modal class? (ii) Median class? (iii)(A) Mean? OR (iii)(B) Mode?
a:
Ans:

  • (i) Highest frequency 15, so modal class = 30-40
  • (ii) N = 50, N/2 = 25. Cumulative frequencies 3, 9, 21, 36, 50. 25 first falls in 36, so median class = 30-40
  • (iii)(A) Class marks 5, 15, 25, 35, 45; fx = 15, 90, 300, 525, 630; Σfx = 1560. Mean = 1560/50 = 31.2
  • (iii)(B) l = 30, f1 = 15, f0 = 12, f2 = 14, h = 10. Mode = 30 + [(15 - 12)/(30 - 12 - 14)] × 10 = 30 + (3/4) × 10 = 37.5

q: Q70 ★ (3 marks, 2019) Find the mode: the modal class is 30-40 with frequency 16; the class before has 10 and the class after has 12 (class size 10).
Q71 ★ (5 marks, 2025) Find the missing frequency f if the mean is 18. Hence find the mode. Daily allowance: 11-13: 7, 13-15: 6, 15-17: 9, 17-19: 13, 19-21: f, 21-23: 5, 23-25: 4
Q72 ★ (5 marks, 2026) The median of the following data is 50 and the total frequency is 90. Find p and q. Class: 20-30: p, 30-40: 15, 40-50: 25, 50-60: 20, 60-70: q, 70-80: 8, 80-90: 10
Q73 ★ (MCQ, SQP; 2026 same) Two dice are rolled together. The probability of getting a number less than 4 on each die is: (A) 1/4 (B) 1/9 (C) 1/36 (D) 1/6
a: Ans: (A) 1/4. Each die must show 1, 2 or 3: 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes out of 36. 9/36 = 1/4.

q: Q74 ★ (MCQ, SQP) 2 diamond cards and 4 spade cards are missing from a pack of 52. A card is drawn at random. P(heart) = ? (A) 13/52 (B) 13/46 (C) 11/52 (D) 11/46
a: Ans: (B) 13/46. Cards left = 52 - 6 = 46. All 13 hearts are still there. (2025: P(red face card) from 52 cards = 6/52 = 3/26. 2024: one black card is lost; P(queen of hearts) = 1/51.)

q: Q75 (MCQ, SQP) T-shirts numbered 4 to 99 are in a box. One is taken at random. P(number is a perfect square or a perfect cube) = ? (A) 1/12 (B) 1/32 (C) 11/96 (D) 5/48
a: Ans: (D) 5/48. Total = 96. Squares: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81 (8). Cubes: 8, 27, 64 (3). 64 is counted twice, so favourable = 8 + 3 - 1 = 10. P = 10/96 = 5/48.

q: Q76 (MCQ, 2024; 2023 similar) If the probability of a player winning a game is 0.79, the probability of his losing is:
a: Ans: 0.21 (1 - 0.79). (2023: a girl's probability of winning a lottery prize is 0.08; 6000 tickets were sold, so she bought 0.08 × 6000 = 480 tickets. 2023: 5 of 20 people can't swim, P(can swim) = 15/20 = 3/4.)

q: Q77 (A-R, 2026) A: If the probability of an event is 0.2p, p > 0, then p cannot be more than 5. R: P(not E) = 1 - P(E) for an event E.
a: Ans: (B) Both true, but R does not explain A. (A is true because a probability is at most 1: 0.2p ≤ 1 gives p ≤ 5.)

q: Q78 ★ (2 marks, SQP) Two dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the product of the numbers is a prime number.
a:
Ans:

  • A product is prime only when one die shows 1 and the other a prime: (1,2), (2,1), (1,3), (3,1), (1,5), (5,1) = 6 outcomes
  • P = 6/36 = 1/6

q: Q79 ★ (3 marks, 2025; 2017 similar) Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability that the difference of the numbers on the two dice is 2.
a:
Ans:

  • Favourable: (1,3), (3,1), (2,4), (4,2), (3,5), (5,3), (4,6), (6,4) = 8
  • P = 8/36 = 2/9 (2017: sum less than 7: 15 outcomes, P = 5/12; product less than 16: 25 outcomes, P = 25/36; doublet of odd numbers (1,1), (3,3), (5,5): P = 3/36 = 1/12. 2024 MCQ: sum 2, 3 or 5: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 outcomes, P = 7/36.)

q: Q80 ★ (2 marks, 2019) A game consists of tossing a coin 3 times and noting the outcome each time. Getting the same result in all tosses is a success. Find the probability of losing the game.
a:
Ans:

  • Outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT = 8
  • Success: HHH, TTT = 2. P(win) = 2/8 = 1/4
  • P(lose) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4 (2019: a die is thrown once; P(prime) = 3/6 = 1/2; P(number between 2 and 6, i.e. 3, 4, 5) = 1/2. 2023: bag with 4 red, 3 blue, 2 yellow balls; P(yellow) = 2/9, P(red) = 4/9.)
